matrix.description: 默认环境，不加载额外插件，用于观察原生 DSH 能力。

session.assistantText:
Goal: read the pstack role model config file, list its role routes, and dispatch one executor under a configured role.

**The config file exists.** It lives at `$DSH_HOME/pstack-models.mdc` (`$DSH_HOME` is `<HOST_PATH> This is the one file `pstack_subagent` re-reads on every delegation, and base DSH never loads it as a rule.

**Roles it defines.** Two of the manifest's 18 roles carry a route. Every other role inherits the parent route.

- `bug-fix` → `magpie/workbuddy/deepseek-v4.1-flash` with effort `low`
- `judgment and prose` → `magpie/workbuddy/minimax-m3.1-flash` with effort `high`

The manifest itself lists these shapes. Single roles take `roleIndex: null`. `arena runners`, `architect runners`, and `interrogate reviewers` are automatic panels that fan out one child per list entry. `arena cross-judge pool` and `swarm workers` take a `roleIndex` to select one entry.

**The executor I dispatched.** I picked `bug-fix`, a role the file explicitly configures. The child resolved to route `magpie/workbuddy/deepseek-v4.1-flash` at effort `low`, matching the file line exactly. It read the config and reported the same two roles. I confirmed its output myself against the file.

**One note.** The workspace README.md does not contain the role routes. It only names the probe and describes the task, so it is a task description rather than a copy of the config. If you wanted the README to be the config source, that file is still to be written.

**What the next engineer inherits.** The role file is the single point of truth for delegation routes. Editing it affects the next child, never a running one, so changes are safe to make mid-session.
